feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform leadership, with clear domain focus, solid progression, and relevant technical breadth. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with limited outcome-focused evidence beyond scope and activity.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline and summary immediately establish a strong niche in public-sector digital platforms, governance, and communications systems.  
- Credible career progression: long tenure at NACo with steady advancement supports leadership credibility and subject-matter depth.  
- Good specificity: strong tools/platform detail (Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Clarity, Power BI, AI search) and useful scale indicators like 10,000+ pages and 3.5 million annual page views.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than impact. Include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign performance.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve structure and scannability.  
- Tighten style consistency: minor punctuation/style inconsistencies appear, e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. lists without the serial comma, and “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler in Education. No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and adding one sharper differentiator would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider a more concise version: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise website transformation, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct action verbs like “modernizing,” “scaling,” or “leading” to sound more executive.
- Use parallel structure in the second sentence; the current list mixes systems, functions, and outputs.
- If space allows, add one concrete scope marker from recent roles, such as “10,000+ page websites” or “50+ internal publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it broad here unless you remove detail elsewhere.
- “Governance models/content operations/editorial systems” are closely related; streamline to avoid stacking similar concepts.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and weighted toward higher-level leadership capabilities over detailed execution areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use tighter, parallel phrasing and emphasize strategic scope: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • Cross-channel communications leadership
- Keep the most differentiating strengths near the front: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications
- Simplify the final item for consistency: Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Consider trimming to 6–7 items to avoid reading like a second skills section

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” are already prominent in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Digital governance & editorial systems” overlaps with both the header and multiple NACo role bullets.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work experience. Tightening phrasing, standardizing style, and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it more impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency; use parallel verb structure for all entries.
- Tighten wording: “bill-level AI chat” could become “AI chat at the bill level,” and “continued campaign growth” could be “future campaign expansion.”
- Consider a cleaner rewrite: “Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.”
- Standardize formatting and punctuation across entries; keep each project to one crisp outcome-focused line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in NACo roles.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item; consider prioritizing unique projects here and trimming repeats from this footer.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning in 2024.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + level: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, Drupal platform enhancements, and cross-channel communications systems.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Consolidate build work into one sharper bullet: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Keep the AI/search bullet, but make it the differentiator: “Lead an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- Specific microsite/campaign examples may be better left to Recent Projects unless you can add measurable results here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize executive ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s channel-management details. Lead with the website modernization and analytics/governance wins.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a national membership organization.”
- Combine and sharpen the website bullet: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit: add results for analytics/governance/video where possible (e.g., reporting speed, stakeholder adoption, production cost savings, turnaround time, publishing consistency).
- Replace softer phrasing like “strengthened”/“expanded” with outcome verbs: “standardized publishing governance,” “built enterprise reporting infrastructure,” “launched first in-house broadcast studio.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and systems.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo bullets unless framed here as building organizational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads broad and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around executional leadership, channel ownership, and systems/process improvements, with any concrete audience or production metrics you can add.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Make bullets more action/result focused:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Coordinated editorial calendars and campaign execution across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and cross-team coordination.
- If possible, add metrics: newsletter open/click rates, video cadence/views, publishing volume, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed” or “oversaw execution” here instead of “led.”
- Video program language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects; keep this version focused on scaling/operationalizing it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skill block overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and outcomes-oriented leadership rather than generic phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, executive-level wording: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Content governance & editorial operations,” “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “Public-sector advocacy messaging,” “Audience strategy & content planning.”
- Consider adding one impact cue in the heading or nearby summary, e.g., “Led strategy for 10,000+ page Drupal migration and 3.5M annual page views,” rather than keeping this section purely generic.
- Use parallel noun phrases and avoid filler like “focused”; “Audience strategy & content planning” is stronger than “Audience-focused content planning.”
- If space allows, make “Multi-channel” more specific: “Web, email, social & multimedia leadership.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Editorial systems and governance” is already well evidenced in recent NACo experience; avoid restating it elsewhere without added specificity.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, make it more outcome-oriented and emphasize the most relevant recent strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal and CMS modernization first; they are most supported by recent NACo work. Consider dropping or de-emphasizing older/less evidenced platforms like WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages here.
- Replace “technical execution” jargon with clearer value language such as “web platform delivery” or “CMS and web implementation.”
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “enterprise web platforms” or “large public-facing sites” to connect to the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep this section higher-level and save full tool inventory for the technical section.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster that aligns with the most recent NACo leadership work, but it reads as a raw tool list. Tighten it into outcome-oriented capabilities and reduce overlap with broader “Data analytics & reporting” language elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first: “Digital analytics & optimization: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery”
- Replace generic items with sharper business value: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive dashboards and decision support”
- Tighten “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX, and content performance analysis”
- Consider adding impact language if style allows: “KPI framework design, executive dashboards, and insight generation for web and campaign optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “KPI design” and “Leadership reporting” overlap with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and analytics infrastructure in the Director role.
- Tool list duplicates the Director of Digital Media bullet; keep this section concise and capability-led rather than repeating the same stack verbatim.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with work-experience bullets about the in-house studio, livestreams, and video programming. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and clearer production scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrasing with more senior, outcome-oriented terms: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Live and hybrid event production,” “Studio and control-room operations.”
- Reorder by strategic value and recency: lead with live/hybrid production and studio leadership, then technical tools like PTZ.
- Consider a tighter version: “- Live, hybrid, and virtual event production - Broadcast-quality video production and editing - Studio and control-room operations - Livestreaming and PTZ camera systems”
- If possible elsewhere on the CV, support this with scale metrics (events produced, audience size, frequency of livestreams) rather than listing too many sub-skills here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with Core Competencies (“Multimedia & live event production”); keep one broader and this one more technical.
- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” are closely related; combine to save space.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Since Drupal is clearly the strongest/recent platform, lead with that emphasis or trim this item to avoid repeating the same story.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider signaling depth: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal site builds/migrations • WordPress administration • SharePoint intranets • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Keep platform names only; avoid mixing in broader capabilities here since those already appear elsewhere.
- If this section should feel more senior, consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one or making this version more platform-specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so don’t overstate older/less central platforms without context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. It should emphasize current, implementation-level tools and group them more cleanly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second grouped phrase: “Technical tools: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, make it more outcome-oriented by tying tools to use cases elsewhere in the CV, e.g. “API integrations for CMS/content workflows” or “GitHub Actions for deployment automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless you need ATS keyword matching; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”); avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places
- “Workflow automation” already appears in Topline Skills [2], so use “GitHub Actions” and “Cloudflare Workers” here to add specificity rather than repeat automation language

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is useful, but it currently reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps with stronger “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” language elsewhere. Make it tighter and more senior by separating true automation platforms from collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just listing tools: **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp (project workflows) • Slack/Teams (cross-team coordination)**
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value tools if this section feels crowded; emphasize platforms tied to systems design rather than basic workplace software.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; they add less differentiation than Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it’s currently just a vendor list with no signal on depth or relevance. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize platform fluency rather than repeat “email” generally.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten content to: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of more tools: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member communications) • Mailchimp (newsletter deployment)
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, list it first to reflect recency and strength.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding phrases like “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or “campaign strategy” here; those are already covered in recent Work Experience.
- Don’t expand this into outcomes unless you can tie each platform to a distinct achievement not already stated elsewhere.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo Director bullet. Tighten it to emphasize applied capability rather than a second list of the same platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Replace “Dashboarding” with a more specific capability such as **KPI reporting** or **Executive dashboards**
- Consider tightening to: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- If space allows elsewhere, move impact into recent experience instead of here, e.g., analytics stack “supporting leadership reporting and decision-making”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; keep one version broader and this one strictly tool-focused
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating extra descriptors here

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles on workflows, weekly video, and team leadership. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize “firsts” or scale from this earlier stage.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and multimedia communications.”
- Split the second sentence into concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video content, and helped formalize cross-channel production workflows.”
- Replace “high-impact” and “strengthening” with specifics; add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos, audience growth, production cadence, or size/timing of the site refresh.
- Soften management language unless it was formal: change “providing day-to-day guidance” to “coordinating or mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this item as launching or early-building the format.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this version tactical, not strategic.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize coordination + launch impact, and keep it lean since more recent NACo roles carry the stronger digital leadership story.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the clearest outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; partnered on digital and multimedia content to extend member-facing communications.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and more results-oriented: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If you can, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.
- Consider trimming “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials,” which is vague; replace with specific outputs or channels.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid overemphasizing multimedia production here; later roles already establish video/content leadership more strongly.
- “First podcast” is distinctive—keep that, but don’t repeat broad digital-team language used in 2015–2024 entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads a bit dated and overlaps with stronger, higher-level multimedia claims elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools/software only, and avoid repeating production capabilities already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
